entries.name: Coconut palm
entries.leaves: evergreen, huge pinnate fronds arching from a single crown
entries.flowers: small, creamy, on long branched spikes, twice a year or more
entries.fruit: coconut: a large buoyant drupe with drinkable water and rich flesh; germinates years after washing ashore
entries.voxel_shape: one tall slender grey trunk, usually leaning seaward, crowned by a burst of feathery fronds
entries.notes: The archetypal beach tree: unmistakable silhouette, and its drifting fruit colonises new shores. Gives shade, food and drink within minutes of a survivor's needs.

entries.name: Sea almond
entries.leaves: large, obovate, leathery, 15–25 cm; turn pink-red before dropping in the dry season
entries.flowers: small, white-green, in short spikes, inconspicuous
entries.fruit: corky 5–7 cm drupe, yellow to red when ripe, edible kernel inside
entries.voxel_shape: tiered, pagoda-like crown of broad almond-shaped leaves on horizontal branches
entries.notes: The big tiered tree of tropical shores. Leaves flush red and fall out of season; the corky seed drifts across oceans and sprouts on bare sand.

entries.name: Tamanu
entries.leaves: glossy, dark green, opposite, with fine parallel side veins; evergreen
entries.flowers: white, sweetly fragrant, in panicles, much of the year
entries.fruit: round 2–4 cm green drupe ('ballnut'), seed crushed for tamanu oil
entries.voxel_shape: broad irregular crown on heavy arching limbs that reach over the water
entries.notes: The sacred tree of Austronesian voyaging: spread hand-to-hand across Oceania for its timber and its healing oil; as important to Pacific shipwrights as oak to Europe.

entries.name: Portia tree
entries.leaves: heart-shaped, glossy, 8–20 cm
entries.flowers: yellow hibiscus-like, dark at the throat
entries.fruit: dry, leathery, brittle capsule
entries.voxel_shape: compact, dense rounded crown of glossy foliage
entries.notes: One of the great Austronesian canoe plants, carried across the Pacific; its fine-grained reddish wood turns beautiful umeke bowls.

entries.name: Fish poison tree
entries.leaves: obovate, glossy, waxy, to 40 cm long
entries.flowers: large, fragrant, white-pink, 15 cm across, opening at night
entries.fruit: large pyramidal woody fruit, buoyant, floats for years
entries.voxel_shape: low spreading crown with enormous glossy leaves and big white night flowers
entries.notes: The beach pioneer carried by the currents: fruits drift for years, and it colonised new islands after eruptions like Krakatau. Seeds and bark stun fish.

entries.name: Beach screwpine
entries.leaves: long, sword-like, with spiny margins, spirally arranged at branch tips
entries.flowers: male: scented hanging catkins; female: dense heads
entries.fruit: large cluster of woody key-like segments, edible and fibrous
entries.voxel_shape: trunk propped on arching stilt roots, tufted with spiral crowns of spiny leaves
entries.notes: The Pacific islet tree on stilt roots: keys of fruit, pineapple-like crowns of spiny leaves; leaves woven into everything from mats to sails.

entries.name: Sea grape
entries.leaves: very large, round, leathery, pale-veined, like grape leaves
entries.flowers: small, white-green, in long racemes
entries.fruit: round, 1 cm, purple when ripe, in grape-like clusters; tart, edible
entries.voxel_shape: broad gnarled low tree with huge round leaves and hanging grape clusters
entries.notes: Caribbean beach staple: tart grapes eaten straight off the stem; the enormous round leaves laugh at salt spray and hurricane winds.

entries.name: Sea hibiscus
entries.leaves: heart-shaped, glossy, to 15 cm, palmately veined
entries.flowers: large hibiscus-like, yellow with a dark red centre, fading orange by evening
entries.fruit: dry, brittle capsule with hairy seeds
entries.voxel_shape: spreading dense crown, glossy leaves, yellow flowers that age to rust
entries.notes: The yellow 'cottonwood' of Pacific and Indian Ocean shores; its bark was spun into the cordage for outrigger canoes and fishing nets.

entries.name: Coastal sheoak
entries.leaves: reduced to tiny scale whorls; long drooping jointed branchlets act as leaves
entries.flowers: tiny catkin-like spikes, wind-pollinated
entries.fruit: small oval woody cone with winged samaras
entries.voxel_shape: tall conifer-like silhouette of fine weeping grey-green needle branchlets
entries.notes: Whistles in the sea breeze and fixes its own nitrogen, so it colonises bare sand; planted densely it builds a living sea wall. Occasionally to 35 m.

entries.name: Coast banksia
entries.leaves: narrow, stiff, serrated, glossy above, pale beneath, to 20 cm
entries.flowers: large cylindrical spikes of yellow-cream florets, very honey-rich
entries.fruit: woody follicles clustered on a woody cone; seed held for years
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled dense small tree with upright candles of yellow flower spikes
entries.notes: The eastern Australian foreshore bank: flower candles thick with honey, and cones that only release their seed when fire passes through.

entries.name: Norfolk Island pine
entries.leaves: soft, awl-like on young trees; small curved scales on mature branches; evergreen
entries.flowers: sexes on separate trees; male cones yellow, female globose
entries.fruit: large globose cones, 10–12 cm, disintegrating at maturity
entries.voxel_shape: enormous symmetrical conifer with tiers of five horizontal branches
entries.notes: The perfect tropical beach icon, planted on warm shores worldwide; wild only on Norfolk Island. Native trees in Hawaii are actually its relative, the Cook pine.

entries.name: Maritime pine
entries.leaves: needles in pairs, long, to 22 cm, dark green
entries.flowers: male cones yellow-orange; female cones reddish
entries.fruit: large conical cones, 8–18 cm, maturing over two years
entries.voxel_shape: tall pine with a broad, slightly domed crown on Atlantic dune sand
entries.notes: The tree that anchored the Landes of southwest France: millions planted to pin down the marching dunes between Bordeaux and the Pyrenees.

entries.name: Stone pine
entries.leaves: needles in pairs, long, grey-green
entries.flowers: male cones yellow; female cones green
entries.fruit: large round cones holding edible pine nuts
entries.voxel_shape: flat-topped umbrella canopy held high on a thick trunk
entries.notes: Rome's umbrella pine: its broad dishes of canopy shade Mediterranean beaches, and its cones stock the pine kernels of pesto.

entries.name: Tamarisk
entries.leaves: tiny, scale-like, feathery, grey-green; twigs almost leafless
entries.flowers: pink plumes, small, in summer
entries.fruit: tiny capsule releasing wind-blown seed
entries.voxel_shape: feathery plume shrub, soft pink mists of flower in summer
entries.notes: The briniest plant on the beach: drinks brackish water and sweats the salt out through its leaves, surviving straight spray and wrack lines.

entries.name: Sea buckthorn
entries.leaves: narrow, silvery-grey, underside felted in starry scales
entries.flowers: small, brownish, before the leaves
entries.fruit: small orange drupes in dense clusters; very sour, supremely vitamin-C-rich
entries.voxel_shape: silvery spiny thicket studded with orange berry beads
entries.notes: The berry of the Baltic dunes: mouth-puckering orange pearls packed with vitamin C, behind walls of silver spines.

entries.name: Coastal wattle
entries.leaves: phyllodes (flattened leaf-like stalks), sickle-shaped, grey-green
entries.flowers: bright yellow globular puffballs in late winter–spring
entries.fruit: dark coiled pods with hard seeds
entries.fire: resprouts from base and root suckers
entries.voxel_shape: dense dark mound of foliage flaring yellow in spring
entries.notes: The spring firework of Australian foredunes: whole dune ridges smoke yellow with flower just before the first gales.

entries.name: Beach rose
entries.leaves: wrinkled (rugose), glossy dark green, grey-felted beneath, thorny stems
entries.flowers: large, fragrant, magenta to white, crinkled petals, summer to autumn
entries.fruit: big red hips, rich in vitamin C
entries.voxel_shape: low thorny thicket crammed with crinkled pink flowers and red hips
entries.notes: Native to Japan and East Asia, run rampant on northern Atlantic and Pacific dunes; the hips make famously good jelly.

entries.name: Beach naupaka
entries.leaves: spoon-shaped, glossy, fleshy, clustered at branch tips
entries.flowers: white 'half flowers' (fan of petals on one side only)
entries.fruit: white berry, buoyant
entries.voxel_shape: bushy rounded shrub with all leaves clustered at the twig ends
entries.notes: The 'split flower' of the Pacific shore: each bloom is a single fan. White berries float ashore and keep the strandline green.

entries.name: Bay cedar
entries.leaves: narrow, silvery-grey, succulent-leathery, spirally crowded at tips
entries.flowers: small, yellow, scattered year-round
entries.fruit: small dry capsule
entries.voxel_shape: compact low grey cushion of foliage in the wrack line
entries.notes: The grey pioneer sitting right on the wrack line from Florida to the Indian Ocean; first green thing past the debris.

entries.name: Railroad vine
entries.leaves: two-lobed (goat-foot), leathery, shiny, on long stems that run down the beach
entries.flowers: purple-pink funnels, morning glory, open in the morning
entries.fruit: small capsule of hard black seeds
entries.voxel_shape: long parallel runners carpeting the foredune, studded with pink trumpets
entries.notes: The railroad vine: stems run ruler-straight down the beach and root at the nodes — one plant, one endless line of track.

entries.name: Sea bindweed
entries.leaves: kidney-shaped, fleshy, long-stalked, lying flat on sand
entries.flowers: bells striped pink and white, late spring to autumn
entries.fruit: dry capsule
entries.voxel_shape: fleshy kidney-leaf mat with pink-striped bell flowers
entries.notes: Europe's dune convolver: a carpet of shiny kidney leaves punched through with candy-striped bells, thriving on the most mobile sand.

entries.name: Beach bean
entries.leaves: trifoliate, tough, rounded leaflets
entries.flowers: pink-purple pea flowers in racemes
entries.fruit: pod ('beach jackbean') with large seeds
entries.voxel_shape: long trailing legume runners with rounded leaf triplets and pea flowers
entries.notes: The pantropical beach jackbean: a deep-rooted trailing legume whose runners stitch the wrack line together.

entries.name: Hottentot fig
entries.leaves: three-angled, fleshy, bright green, curving upward at tips
entries.flowers: large daisy-like, magenta to yellow, spring to summer
entries.fruit: fig-like, edible, salt-sweet when over-ripe
entries.voxel_shape: dense carpets of three-angled leaves roped across the dunes
entries.notes: South Africa's dune ice plant, exported as a sand-fixer on every continent; it smothers native dune flora worse than any plant it replaced.

entries.name: Marram grass
entries.leaves: grey-green, tightly rolled, stiff, narrow
entries.flowers: dense spike, 15 cm, summer
entries.fruit: small grass caryopsis
entries.voxel_shape: stiff upright tufts in the regular rows of an engineered dune
entries.notes: The engineer's grass: planted by the kilometre to build dunes that out-pace the tide; runners 50 cm a year of new sand.

entries.name: American beachgrass
entries.leaves: grey-green, rolled, with a tiny ligule
entries.flowers: dense spike, late summer
entries.fruit: small caryopsis
entries.voxel_shape: dense clumps of sword-green blades binding the Atlantic dunes
entries.notes: North America's own marram: planting grids of it are how the US Corps of Engineers rebuilds the dunes after nor'easters.

entries.name: Lyme grass
entries.leaves: flat to rolled, glaucous blue-grey, waxy bloom
entries.flowers: thick spike, blue-toned, summer
entries.fruit: caryopsis
entries.voxel_shape: blue-grey blades in loose open tufts on Baltic and North Sea foredunes
entries.notes: The blue-grey lyme of northern Europe's exposed coasts; hardier than marram and twice as cold-tolerant.

entries.name: American dunegrass
entries.leaves: bluish-green, flat to tightly rolled, waxy
entries.flowers: spike, summer
entries.fruit: caryopsis
entries.voxel_shape: silvery blue tufts marching up the Pacific dune faces
entries.notes: The Pacific counterpart to marram: great grey-green colonies on the outermost dunes from Alaska to California.

entries.name: Sea oats
entries.leaves: long, arching, ribbon-like, glossy green
entries.flowers: nodding drooping panicles of flattened seed clusters, autumn
entries.fruit: flattened caryopsis, wind-borne off the beach
entries.voxel_shape: fountain arches of green straps with dangling oat-like plumes
entries.notes: The emblem of the south-eastern US beaches: its flat seed plumes sway like oat sprays and lie flat against the wind.

entries.name: Beach spinifex
entries.leaves: silvery, silky-pubescent, tightly rolled, in dense tufts
entries.flowers: globular bur-like heads that detach and roll down the beach
entries.fruit: caryopsis inside a spinning bur
entries.voxel_shape: low silvery mounds with tumbling bur balls at the strand line
entries.notes: The dunes themselves are built by it: stolons run 30 m and mound the sand; the spinning burs ride the wind along the beach.

entries.name: Pīngao
entries.leaves: stiff, 2–5 mm wide, bright green maturing to golden and orange, spirally arranged
entries.flowers: dark brown spikelets spiralling round the culm, spring
entries.fruit: small dark brown nutlet
entries.voxel_shape: low ropey orange-green sedge tufts running on long stolons
entries.notes: Aotearoa's golden sedge: Māori treasure plant whose bright orange runners were woven into tukutuku panels; displaced by marram grass.

entries.name: Sand sedge
entries.leaves: narrow, grass-like, shiny green
entries.flowers: brown spikelets, summer
entries.fruit: small achene
entries.voxel_shape: thin bright green blades threading out of bare sand on long runners
entries.notes: The sand sedge: metres of white runners knit the foredune together just above the highest tides. (A sedge, not a grass.)

entries.name: Beach pea
entries.leaves: fleshy leaflets in pairs, tipped with a branched tendril
entries.flowers: purple to magenta pea flowers, summer
entries.fruit: flat pod, young ones edible
entries.voxel_shape: low trailing tangle of tendrils and purple pea flowers
entries.notes: The circumpolar beach pea: subarctic beaches flare purple with it; leaves are waxy to survive cold salt spray.

entries.name: Sea rocket
entries.leaves: succulent, lobed, fleshy
entries.flowers: small, lilac to white, cross-shaped (mustard family)
entries.fruit: two-chambered pod that breaks into rocket-like seglets
entries.voxel_shape: low sprawling succulent tufts on open sand with lilac crosses
entries.notes: The rocket launches itself: the ripe pod splits in two, the upper half blasts away on the wind, and the beach gardens itself.

entries.name: Sea kale
entries.leaves: large, wavy-edged, fleshy, glaucous blue-grey; thick taproot
entries.flowers: white, cross-shaped, in big open sprays, early summer
entries.fruit: round corky berry that floats
entries.voxel_shape: big blue-grey cabbage rosettes on shingle with white cauliflower-like sprays
entries.notes: The Victorian dinner-party cabbage of the shingle beach: forced pale shoots were a fashionable delicacy into the 1900s.

entries.name: Sea holly
entries.leaves: spiny, holly-like, stiff, blue-grey, palmately lobed
entries.flowers: steel-blue spiky cone-heads, summer
entries.fruit: small dry achene
entries.voxel_shape: thistle-blue spiny rosettes topped with steel-blue pincushions
entries.notes: The steel-blue thistle of the pebble beach: holly-hard leaves, metallic cone flowers, and a taproot reaching the fresh water under the sand.

entries.name: Sea daffodil
entries.leaves: strap-like, grey-green, appearing after flower
entries.flowers: large, fragrant, white, daffodil-like, late summer; opens at dusk
entries.fruit: large capsule with black seeds
entries.voxel_shape: bare stems crowned with big white fragrant trumpets on empty sand
entries.notes: Blooms on bare, baking Mediterranean sand in late summer; traded since antiquity as a lucky charm — and it smells divine at dusk.

entries.name: Yellow horned poppy
entries.leaves: glaucous, lobed, clasping, blue-grey
entries.flowers: large crumpled yellow poppies with dark spots at the base
entries.fruit: long slender horn-like capsule, to 25 cm
entries.voxel_shape: clumps of glaucous rosettes with big yellow poppy faces and long horns
entries.notes: The brassy cousin of the corn poppy on pebble beaches: seed capsules like long yellow horns; hugs the drift line of shingle.

entries.name: Sea spurge
entries.leaves: fleshy, blue-grey, egg-shaped, spirally arranged
entries.flowers: tiny yellow-green cup-like cyathia, summer
entries.fruit: small capsule
entries.voxel_shape: low fleshy blue-grey columns on the foredune with lime-green tips
entries.notes: The classic foredune pioneer of European shores: armed with blistering white latex, but exactly where the sand first starts to hold.
